requirement: A `{req}` opening fence MAY contain four or more colons. Habeas MUST accept opening fences of any length of at least three colons. A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener MUST remain inside the requirement body, allowing a nested colon directive. A closing fence outside a fenced code example with at least as many colons as the opener MUST end the body.
rationale:
The tests cover every MUST clause in `requirements.ci.fence_lengths`. The MAY clause on four or more colons imposes nothing to check.

- **Openers of at least three colons.**
  - Three colons: `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text]` and `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[markdown_fences_close_with_enough_colons_and_skip_code]`.
  - Four colons: `validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers` in `src/evidence.rs`, and `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive]`.
  - Seven colons: `validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers`.
  - Four and six colons (examples): `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[example_bodies_keep_nested_markdown_and_trim_outer_whitespace]`.
  - The evidence fixtures record the exact body, so a parser that rejected a fence or cut the body short would produce a validation error or a body mismatch. The tests assert that errors are empty, or that the body text equals the expected value.
- **A shorter colon-only line stays in the body.**
  - The three-colon `:::{note}` and `:::` pair nested in a four-colon `{req}` is asserted as part of the body in `validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers`.
  - The same pair sits inside four-colon openers in `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` (`src/lib.rs`), which asserts the exact body text and that the block is closed.
  - It also appears inside the four-colon example in `example_bodies_keep_nested_markdown_and_trim_outer_whitespace`.
  - `markdown_fences_close_with_enough_colons_and_skip_code` checks that a nested `:::{impl}` and its `:::` closer stay in the outer `::::` body.
  - The four-colon opener against a three-colon line is the boundary case that matters, and it is covered.
- **A closer with at least as many colons ends the body.**
  - Equal length: `::::`/`::::` and `:::`/`:::`.
  - Longer: `::::`/`:::::` and `:::::::`/`::::::::`. The same tests also assert that text after the closer is excluded.
  - A five-colon closer after a three-colon opener is asserted in `markdown_fences_close_with_enough_colons_and_skip_code`.
- **Closers inside a fenced code example do not end the body.**
  - In `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text`, the body holds a ```` ```text ```` block containing `:::`, and the whole body must be recorded.
  - `markdown_fences_close_with_enough_colons_and_skip_code` and `example_bodies_keep_nested_markdown_and_trim_outer_whitespace` also cover code-fence skipping, with a literal `:::{example}` or `:::{cite}` inside a code fence.

The assertions check exact body text, the closed flag, counts and absence of errors. They would catch both early termination and failure to terminate. I found no unexercised obligation.
